riskAssessment.reason: Entry pages are reader-facing governance surfaces; broken routes or language drift can block non-technical understanding without changing runtime behavior.

reasons: Initial Work Item skeleton defaults to Standard until scope is classified.

executionDecision.reason: The user explicitly authorized execution of the accepted documentation plan and requested that the authorization be recorded in the Contract.

preReviewWarnings: Do not present planned P0 destinations as complete multilingual content.
Every home must expose the same narrative order and same-language next steps.
A missing localized destination must be labelled as planned rather than silently falling back to English.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: docs/README.md, docs/README.ja.md, and docs/README.zh-CN.md exist and present the same ordered core narrative: North Star/identity, purpose, philosophy, architecture, boundaries, decisions, adoption, and recovery.
README.md, README.ja.md, and README.zh-CN.md link to their matching documentation home and no longer require a reader to silently switch language for the entry journey.
Each localized home exposes reader-goal navigation for understanding, adoption, first use, review, recovery, and maintenance; P0 destinations are reachable from the home in at most two links.
Planned untranslated P0 destinations are visible with an explicit planned/migration label, while currently available same-language pages remain the default route.
Automated tests verify home existence, narrative ordering, language-switch links, same-language entry links, and absence of archive links; focused documentation checks pass.
guidelines: Write for a non-technical reader first; place specialist references after the guided path.
Keep English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese section order and decision boundaries semantically aligned.
Do not claim P0 multilingual completion while registry topics remain planned.
Do not link the entry journey to docs/archive/ or use historical material as current instruction.
Keep links language-local unless an explicit planned English fallback is labelled.

intent.problem: Important project understanding is hidden behind directory-based links and the existing localized READMEs silently fall back to English for key destinations. Non-technical readers need a clear, language-local route from project identity to purpose, architecture, boundaries, first use, and recovery.
constraints: This Work Item creates entry homes and navigation only; complete P0 content migration is subsequent work.
Japanese and Simplified Chinese pages must be useful without claiming every deep document is fully translated.
North Star, philosophy, architecture, and responsibility boundaries must remain visible as project core concepts.
Preserve the existing documentation authority boundary and exclude historical archives from current routes.
intent.rationale: A reader-goal home makes the project understandable before technical reference is required and gives later P0 content Work Items an explicit, testable destination map.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A non-technical reader opens the English, Japanese, or Simplified Chinese root README.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The reader reaches a matching-language documentation home and can follow the same ordered understanding journey without a silent language switch.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Home structure tests inspect root README links and localized section order.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A reader needs architecture, boundaries, first use, or recovery from a localized home.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The destination is visible in the reader-goal navigation within two links, and planned gaps are explicitly labelled.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Link graph tests resolve current paths, reject archive links, and assert planned-gap labels.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: No restricted governance paths are in scope.
